findings.text: One of the twenty-two call sites is never executed by the gate that proves the change, so the arity check reaches 21 of 22 sites and not all 22. VERDICT: NIT on the evidence, not on the code. The site at line 1074 is owned by test_review_release_projects_terminal_name_from_sources, which carries @pytest.mark.graph at line 1051; the repo's default addopts deselect that marker, and both the node's logs confirm it -- baseline_focused.log and after_focused.log each open with 'collected 53 items / 1 deselected / 52 selected', and I reproduced the identity of the deselected test by differencing a default collect against a marker-free collect: it is exactly that test. Python's missing-argument TypeError is a call-time binding check, so it protects a site only when that site runs; this one ran at neither revision. I verified the site by inspection instead, parsing the file's AST: all 22 calls to _stub_exporter pass all_gates_passed, every value is the Constant literal True, and each call sits in a distinct test function. TRIGGERING INPUT: a future edit that drops or mistypes the verdict argument at line 1074 -- the focused gate the node ran, and the default marker set every later gate will use, both stay green at 52 passed; the error surfaces only under 'pytest -m graph' against a live Neo4j, which I confirmed collects that test 1/53. WHAT A NEW TEST INHERITS: an unmarked test added to this file tomorrow cannot call _stub_exporter({}) without an immediate TypeError, so the protection is real and inherited; a test added with @pytest.mark.graph inherits the same blind spot as line 1074.

Seven of the twenty-two newly explicit verdicts are inert by construction: the double they configure is never called. VERDICT: NIT, legibility only. Parsing the file, seven of the 22 owning tests pass dry_run=True to run_review_release (lines 818, 861, 971, 1008, 1873, 1897, 1919). catalog_release.py returns from the dry-run branch at :1990, before the export leg at :1994 and well before the verdict read at :2008; and inside that branch the injected exporter is skipped outright -- :1974 runs the accounting rehearsal only 'if exporter is _default_exporter'. The tests themselves prove it: test_review_release_dry_run_no_push_no_pr asserts 'record == {}' at line 830, i.e. that the stub was never invoked. So at those seven sites the stated verdict is a value handed to a callable that never executes. TRIGGERING INPUT: none that produces a wrong result -- this cannot fail, which is why it is a note. The cost is that a reader of these seven sites infers the export verdict is exercised on the dry-run path when the export leg is not reached at all; the 15 sites that do reach the read at :2008 are the ones where the explicit value carries information.

The prior NIT is genuinely closed for the shared double, but the identical shape survives twice inside this same file. VERDICT: NIT, and I am calling the earlier finding CLOSED rather than moved. The earlier review's concern was specific and propagating: _stub_exporter is a module-level factory, so one edit supplied a passing verdict to every test that used it and a future author inherited it without stating it. That is fixed at the root -- the parameter is required, has no default, and Python refuses the call. What remains is not the same hazard: lines 471-484 (test_review_export_restores_approved_entry_bytes) and 640-660 (the sparse-batch test) define per-test closures that hardcode all_gates_passed=True, each still carrying the 'Export gates are scaffolding; this test exercises ...' comment that the node deleted from _stub_exporter. These are local closures, not a shared factory, so nothing a future test writes can inherit from them -- the blast radius is the one test that owns each. TRIGGERING INPUT: an author copying lines 471-484 as a template for a new export double reproduces the self-supplied verdict, which is a copy-paste risk rather than an inheritance one. Worth one pass to parameterise both for consistency with the file's new idiom; not a reason to hold the node.

Two sibling test files each define their own _stub_exporter that still self-supplies the verdict; both are outside this node's declared write paths and are reported rather than fixed. VERDICT: NIT, and one of the two was already flagged by the earlier review and is still open. test_exclusion_report_is_reachable.py:92 defines 'def _stub_exporter(record)' returning SimpleNamespace with a hardcoded all_gates_passed=True at :110, consumed at :162; test_release_rehearsal_writes_nothing.py:92 defines the same-named factory returning SimpleNamespace(exported_count=...) with no verdict attribute at all, consumed at :146. Because each file defines its own, there is no import route by which this node's required parameter could reach them -- which is also why the node could not have fixed them without widening its fence. TRIGGERING INPUT: for the rehearsal file, change its single run_review_release call at :146 from dry_run=True to a real cut and catalog_release.py:2008-2014 refuses immediately with the missing-verdict error; for the exclusion-report file, the hardcoded True means a test added there inherits a passing verdict exactly as this node's file did before today. Both are red-test or latent outcomes, never a silent false pass in production.

The permissive default still exists one scope further out, in production, and that is by design rather than an oversight. VERDICT: OBSERVATION, no action asked. ExportReport declares 'all_gates_passed: bool = True' at export.py:369, so a report constructed without stating gates claims they passed. I checked whether this is the same defect the wave is removing and concluded it is not: the field is an accumulator that the gate evaluators drive to False (export.py:2777, 2849, 2964, 3197, 3357, 3381), so True is the correct 'no failure recorded yet' identity for an 'all(...)' fold, and the consumer at catalog_release.py:2008-2014 fails closed on a MISSING attribute rather than trusting a default. Recording it because a reader comparing this node's file-scope fix against the production type could reasonably ask, and the answer needs the accumulator argument rather than a grep. TRIGGERING INPUT: none demonstrated; a real one would be a construction site that builds an ExportReport, never runs a gate, and hands it to the release path -- I did not find such a site.

justifications.durability: The chosen shape is the durable one: a required positional parameter with no default, which Python enforces at every call rather than a convention a reviewer must police. Answering point THREE of the measure, I checked every route by which a default could creep back and found none. The signature carries no default value. There is no functools.partial, no wrapper and no factory-of-factories -- grep for 'functools' and 'partial' over the file is empty. tests/standard_names/conftest.py greps clean for both all_gates_passed and _stub_exporter, so no conftest patch supplies one. The file's only fixtures are isnc_repo, the autouse _isolate_release_tests_from_live_dd_gaps monkeypatch (which patches dd_gaps.list_dd_gaps and nothing else), and a graph fixture -- none constructs an exporter. And the value is not a shared module-level constant that every site happens to pass: the AST reports a Constant True literal at all 22 sites, not a Name, so there is no single place a later edit could flip them all. The sibling files define their own same-named factory rather than importing this one, so there is no import route either. Three points deducted, all for what the shape does not buy. Every site passes True, so the refusal path is not exercised at this file scope at all -- I verified it IS covered elsewhere (test_release_gate_verdict_is_read.py:113 and :133, test_export_report_gate.py:60, test_cli_export.py:51 all construct all_gates_passed=False), so this is a division of labour rather than a hole, but this file now states a verdict it never varies. Seven of the 22 stated verdicts are inert because the dry-run branch never calls the injected exporter. And the one graph-marked site shows the enforcement has a tier-shaped blind spot that a future graph-marked test would inherit.
justifications.evidence: The claimed evidence exists, verifies, and could have failed. All three logs are on disk with sha256 digests matching the manifest exactly: baseline_focused.log 4c4615d8..., after_focused.log 498a1641..., negative_control.log fa7ea06e.... Answering point ONE of the measure, I did not take the equality from the report -- I re-ran the focused file at the INTEGRATED head in my own worktree and got '52 passed, 1 deselected, 1 warning in 72.80s' at EXIT=0, identical to both of the worker's revisions (log: logs/head_focused.log). But an unchanged count is weak evidence on its own, exactly as the measure warns, so I corroborated it with two stronger facts. First, value-identity: all 22 sites received True before (hardcoded in the double) and pass True now, so no test could have switched from a refusal to a success. Second, the diff's line arithmetic closes with nothing left over -- 25 deletions = 22 call sites + the def line + the deleted scaffolding comment + the hardcoded 'all_gates_passed=True,' line; 31 insertions = 22 + def + 'all_gates_passed=all_gates_passed,' + 7 docstring lines -- so no assertion line moved anywhere in the file. The negative control is a genuine refusal with the right exit class: its first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim, it ends '1 failed, 52 deselected' with PYTEST_EXIT=1 (a test failure, not a usage error), and the failure is 'TypeError: _stub_exporter() missing 1 required positional argument', which is the guarded thing happening rather than a suite that merely stayed green. Two points deducted for the aperture the manifest does not state: one of the 22 sites (line 1074) is @pytest.mark.graph and deselected by the default addopts, so it executed at NEITHER revision and the 52-passed equality covers 21 of 22 sites; the manifest generalises the single-site negative control to 'the protection is Python's own arity check' without recording that one site is outside the gate's reach. I closed that gap by inspection rather than leaving it open.
justifications.fit: The change reads like the surrounding code and like the paired node it follows. The new docstring states the mechanism and the reason in the file's own register, and the deleted comment ('Export gates are scaffolding; these tests exercise release orchestration') was exactly the assertion the change falsifies, so removing it was right rather than incidental. Keyword form at the call sites (all_gates_passed=True rather than a bare positional True) matches how every other injected double in the file is configured and keeps each site readable at a glance. The node also fits its predecessor correctly: the earlier review's first NIT named this precise hazard at this precise line, and this node closes it at the root -- a future test in this file cannot obtain a passing export verdict without writing one down. One point deducted for the two surviving inline doubles at lines 471 and 640, which now diverge from the file's new idiom and still carry the retired comment, leaving one file with two conventions for the same thing.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node was to make the gate verdict a required parameter of the file-scope release-export double and update every call site, closing at file scope the permissive default the paired guard removed at module scope. It did exactly that and nothing else. At the integrated head daeba4818, 'git show HEAD:tests/standard_names/test_review_release.py' gives 'def _stub_exporter(record, all_gates_passed)' at line 55 with no default, and 22 call sites (23 grep hits minus the def line), each passing all_gates_passed. The claim survived the merge: I verified at HEAD by a marker the change INTRODUCED (the parameter name in the signature), not by the absence of the old form. Answering point TWO of the measure: I checked the VALUE at every site, not merely that a value is present, by parsing the file's AST -- 22 calls, 22 distinct owning test functions, and the value at all 22 is the Constant literal True. No site changed meaning, and structurally none could have: before the change the double hardcoded 'all_gates_passed=True' inside itself with no parameter, so no call site was capable of exercising a refusal. grep confirms no all_gates_passed=False appears in this file at either revision. Deduction of one point: the worker's report describes the file as done while two per-test doubles in the same file (lines 471-484 and 640-660) still hardcode the verdict and still carry the very 'Export gates are scaffolding' comment the node deleted from _stub_exporter; that is a defensible scope call, but it belonged in the report rather than in a reviewer's grep.
justifications.scope_discipline: Exact. The declared write paths were tests/standard_names/test_review_release.py, docs/evidence/archive/unbound-source-backlog-landed.html and docs/plans/unbound-source-backlog.html; 'git show 8ac1b1b2f --stat' reports a single file changed, 31 insertions and 25 deletions, and the two docs land in the separate commit cc1acd9fd. No production file was touched -- I checked what the change could reach and confirmed imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_release.py and export.py are untouched by either commit. The two adjacent temptations were both correctly left alone: the sibling files that define their own _stub_exporter (test_exclusion_report_is_reachable.py:92, test_release_rehearsal_writes_nothing.py:92) are outside the fence, and the node neither widened to them nor silently edited them. Commits are conventional with a body, carry no AI attribution, and name no plan or ticket identifier in the message, the symbol names or the comments -- the new docstring states the mechanism ('the release path refuses an export report that carries no verdict') rather than the plan item. Full marks.
